title: Germany Job Seeker Visa 2026: Opportunity Card Guide
metaDescription: Germany job seeker visa 2026: the Opportunity Card needs 6 points, proof of €1,091 per month, German A1 or English B2, and allows one year to find skilled work.
headline: Germany Job Seeker Visa 2026: the Opportunity Card Explained

sections.title: What the Opportunity Card is
sections.content:
The Opportunity Card, or Chancenkarte, is a job-search residence permit under Section 20a of Germany's Residence Act, available since 1 June 2024. It lets qualified professionals from outside the EU and EFTA live in Germany for up to one year to find skilled work, without needing a job offer first. Germany's older six-month Job Seeker visa has largely been replaced by this card.

The card addresses Germany's need for roughly 400,000 skilled workers a year. During the search year, holders may work part-time for up to 20 hours a week and may do trial work of up to two weeks per employer, without Federal Employment Agency approval. Spouses or partners who also meet the requirements can apply jointly.

sections.title: The points system
sections.content:
There are two ways in. The skilled-worker route applies if you hold a German qualification or a foreign qualification fully recognised in Germany: you skip the points system entirely and need no language certificate. The points route applies if your qualification is not yet fully recognised, and requires at least 6 points plus basic requirements.

Points are awarded for partial recognition of a qualification (4), a shortage occupation (1), at least two years of professional experience in the last five years (2) or five years in the last seven (3), German at A2, B1 or B2 (1, 2 or 3), English at C1 (1), age under 35 (2) or 35 to 40 (1), six months of previous legal residence in Germany (1), and a spouse or partner who also applies (1).

sections.title: Requirements and funds
sections.content:
On the points route you must also show German at A1 level or English at B2 level, and prove you can support yourself with €1,091 per month, or €13,092 for a full year. Proof can come from a blocked account (Sperrkonto), a sponsor's declaration, or a part-time work contract. The national visa fee is €75, and health insurance is required.

Standard processing usually takes 3 to 5 months depending on the German mission and application volume. If you graduated from a German university, a separate job-search permit for graduates under Section 20 of the Residence Act, valid up to 18 months, may apply instead. The official Make it in Germany self-check calculates your score before you apply.

sections.title: After you find a job
sections.content:
Once you secure a qualifying job offer, the Opportunity Card can be converted into an EU Blue Card or a skilled worker visa from inside Germany, without leaving the country. This is the main payoff of the route: you search on the ground, interview in person, and switch to a work permit once hired.

The card can also be extended by up to two years if you hold a qualified job offer and receive Federal Employment Agency approval, even if no other permit fits your situation. Note that the card itself is optional: with a confirmed offer of qualified employment, you can apply for other visa types directly from abroad, which may be faster.

faqs.a: The Opportunity Card, or Chancenkarte, is a job-search residence permit under Section 20a of Germany's Residence Act that has been available since 1 June 2024. It lets qualified non-EU professionals live in Germany for up to one year to find skilled work, without needing a job offer first. Holders may work part-time for up to 20 hours per week.

faqs.q: How many points do I need for the Opportunity Card?
faqs.a: On the points route you need at least 6 points, earned for qualifications, experience, language skills, age, and ties to Germany. Partial recognition of a qualification gives 4 points, five years of experience in the last seven gives 3 points, German at B2 gives 3 points, and being under 35 gives 2 points. Recognized qualifications skip the points system entirely.

faqs.q: How much money do I need to prove for the Opportunity Card?
faqs.a: You must prove funds of €1,091 per month, or €13,092 for a full year, through a blocked account, a sponsor's declaration, or a part-time work contract. Processing usually takes 3 to 5 months depending on the German mission, and the national visa fee is €75. Health insurance is also required for the stay.

faqs.q: What happens after I find a job on the Opportunity Card?
faqs.a: Once you secure a qualifying job offer, the Opportunity Card can be converted into an EU Blue Card or a skilled worker visa from inside Germany. The card can also be extended by up to two years if you hold a qualified job offer and receive Federal Employment Agency approval, even if no other permit fits your situation.
